verses.text: Now a man from the tribe of Levi married a woman who was also from the tribe of Levi.
She became pregnant and had a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful baby, she hid him for three months.

When she could not hide him any longer, she got a basket made of reeds for him and covered it with tar so that water could not get in. She put the baby in it and set it among the tall grass at the edge of the river.
His sister stood some distance away to see what would happen to him.
Then Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river to wash, while her servant girls walked along the river bank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her servant to get it.
She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying, and she felt sorry for him. "This is one of the Hebrew babies," she said.
Then his sister asked Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and find one of the Hebrew women to feed the baby for you?"
"Yes, go," Pharaoh's daughter answered. So the girl went and got the baby's own mother.
Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this baby and feed him for me, and I will pay you." So the woman took the baby and fed him.
When the child grew older, she took him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, because she said, "I pulled him out of the water."
Years later, when Moses had grown up, he went out to visit his own people, the Hebrews, and saw how hard they had to work. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
Moses looked this way and that way, and when he saw that no one was watching, he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
The next day he went out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He asked the one who was in the wrong, "Why are you hitting your fellow Hebrew?"
The man answered, "Who made you our ruler and judge? Are you going to kill me like you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid. He thought, "People must know what I did."
When Pharaoh heard about it, he tried to kill Moses. But Moses ran away from Pharaoh and went to live in the land of Midian. There he sat down beside a well.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came to draw water and fill the drinking troughs for their father's flock.
Some shepherds came and chased them away. But Moses stood up to help them, and he watered their flock.
When the girls went home to their father Reuel, he asked them, "Why are you back so early today?"
They answered, "An Egyptian saved us from the shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the flock."
He asked his daughters, "Where is he? Why did you leave him there? Invite him to come and eat with us."
Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave him his daughter Zipporah to be his wife.
She had a son, and Moses named him Gershom, because he said, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land."
After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The people of Israel groaned because they were slaves, and they cried out. Their cry for help because of their slavery went up to God.
God heard their groaning, and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
God looked at the people of Israel, and he understood what they were going through.
